cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! It's so good to see you again.

cues.caption: Last time: sorting 5, 9, 12, 21, 30
cues.text: Last time, you compared numbers, and sorted toy cars from smallest to biggest. Five, nine, twelve, twenty one, thirty. Remember?

cues.caption: Chapter 4 · Sets
cues.text: Today is chapter four of Logic and Reasoning. It's called, Sets. Things that belong together.

cues.caption: Sort into groups. But what goes where?
cues.text: Sorting by size is one way to tidy up. But sometimes, we sort things into groups instead. Hmm. So how do we decide what goes where?

cues.caption: Let's find out with a messy story!
cues.text: Let's find out, with a very messy little story.

cues.caption: Chintu tipped everything onto the floor!
cues.text: Meet your little cousin, Chintu. Oh no! He's tipped out the fruit basket and the toy box, all over the floor. Mangoes, bananas, a cricket bat, a football, everything!

cues.caption: How would you tidy this up? Think!
cues.text: Mum says, put the things that belong together, back together. How would you tidy this up? Think for a moment.

cues.caption: Fruits → basket · Sports things → toy box
cues.text: The fruits go back in the basket. Mango, banana, apple, guava. And the sports things go in the toy box. Cricket bat, football.

cues.caption: Each group belongs together. Tidy!
cues.text: Ahh, much better! Each group has things that belong together. And now Chintu can find his football in one second.

cues.caption: A group that belongs together = a SET
cues.text: In maths, a group of things that belong together has a special name. It's called a set.

cues.caption: Fruits · Sports things · My school bag
cues.text: So the basket is the set of fruits. The toy box is the set of sports things. Even the things in your school bag make a set!

cues.caption: Mango is a MEMBER of the set "fruits"
cues.text: Each thing inside a set is called a member. Mango is a member of the set, fruits. Is the football a member of fruits? No way! It belongs with the sports things.

cues.caption: Fruits: mango, banana, apple, guava
cues.text: Let's check some sets. Here's the set, fruits. Mango, banana, apple, guava. Yes, they all belong!

cues.caption: Sports: which one doesn't belong?
cues.text: Now, the set, sports. Cricket. Kabaddi. Football. Samosa. Wait a minute! Which one doesn't belong? Think.

cues.caption: Samosa is a snack, not a sport!
cues.text: Samosa! It's yummy, but it's a snack, not a sport. So it doesn't belong in this set. You can't play a match of samosa!

cues.caption: Show a set as a circle: "red things"
cues.text: Here's a neat way to show a set. We draw a big circle, and put its members inside. This circle is the set, red things.

cues.caption: Red apple, red car, red ball → inside
cues.text: A red apple? Inside. A red toy car? Inside. A red ball? Inside too!

cues.caption: Green leaf → outside. It doesn't belong.
cues.text: And a green leaf? It's not red, so it stays outside the circle. Inside means it belongs. Outside means it doesn't.

cues.caption: Two circles = a VENN DIAGRAM
cues.text: Now let's draw two circles that overlap, like this. Circle A is red things. Circle B is round things. This picture is called a Venn diagram.

cues.caption: Red toy car → only A (red)
cues.text: A red toy car. Is it red? Yes. Is it round? No. So it goes only in circle A.

cues.caption: Orange ball → only B (round)
cues.text: An orange ball. Is it red? No. Is it round? Yes! So it goes only in circle B.

cues.caption: Red ball: red AND round. Where?
cues.text: Now, a red ball. It's red, and it's round! So where should it go? Think.

cues.caption: The middle (overlap) = in BOTH sets
cues.text: Right in the middle, where the circles overlap! The overlap is for things that belong to both sets. Red, and round.

cues.caption: Banana: not red, not round → outside
cues.text: And a yellow banana? Is it red? No. Is it round? No. So it goes outside both circles. We call that, neither.

cues.caption: Only A · Only B · Both · Neither
cues.text: So every item gets exactly one spot. Only A. Only B. Both, in the middle. Or neither, outside. Just ask the two questions each time.

cues.caption: A: things you write with · B: made of wood
cues.text: Let's try Chintu's school bag. Circle A is things you write with. Circle B is things made of wood.

cues.caption: Wooden pencil → both → the middle
cues.text: First, a wooden pencil. You write with it, and it's made of wood. Both! So it goes in the middle.

cues.caption: Pen → A · Ruler → B · Bottle → neither
cues.text: A pen? You write with it, but it's plastic. Only A. A wooden ruler? Made of wood, but you don't write with it. Only B. And the water bottle? Neither!

cues.caption: A: yellow things · B: things you eat
cues.text: Now, a sorting game! New circles. Circle A is yellow things. Circle B is things you eat.

cues.caption: Yellow school bus. Where does it go?
cues.text: Here comes a yellow school bus. Where does it go? Think!

cues.caption: Bus → only yellow. You can't eat a bus!
cues.text: Only in yellow things! The bus is yellow, but you definitely can't eat it. Crunch!

cues.caption: Banana → both · Roti → eat · Pencil → neither
cues.text: A banana is yellow, and you can eat it, so it goes in the middle. A roti is food, but it's not yellow, so only things you eat. And a blue pencil? Neither!

cues.caption: A: games with a ball · B: team games
cues.text: Here's a tricky one. Circle A is games played with a ball. Circle B is games played in a team.

cues.caption: Which one goes in the middle?
cues.text: Running race. Chess. Swimming. Football. Which one goes in the middle? Take your time.

cues.caption: Football: ball AND team → the middle!
cues.text: Football! It uses a ball, and you play it in a team. A running race, chess and swimming? No ball, and no team. So they go outside.

cues.caption: Set A: 2, 4, 6, 8 · Set B: 3, 6, 9
cues.text: Sets work with numbers too! Set A is two, four, six, eight. Set B is three, six, nine.

cues.caption: Which number is in BOTH sets?
cues.text: Is there a number that's in both sets? Look carefully.

cues.caption: 6 is in both → it goes in the middle
cues.text: Six! It's in set A, and it's in set B. So six goes in the middle. Two, four and eight stay in A. Three and nine stay in B.

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, practice check time. Just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Red things · Things you eat. An apple?
cues.text: The circles are red things, and things you eat. Where does an apple go? Pause the video, and decide.

cues.caption: Apple → middle: red AND you can eat it
cues.text: In the middle! An apple is red, and you can eat it. So it belongs to both sets. Did you get it? Brilliant!

cues.caption: Red toy car → only red things
cues.text: And Chintu's red toy car? It's red, but please don't eat it! So it goes only in red things. Not the middle.

cues.caption: Set = a group that belongs together
cues.text: Let's remember what we learned. A set is a group of things that belong together.

cues.caption: Each circle is one set
cues.text: In a Venn diagram, each circle is one set.

cues.caption: Middle = in both sets
cues.text: The middle, where the circles overlap, is for things in both sets.

cues.caption: Outside = in neither set
cues.text: And outside the circles means, neither set.

cues.caption: Chapter 4 done!
cues.text: Chapter four, done! You sort things like a real maths detective, champ.

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
